title: Quebec group drug insurance
tagline: A cautious answer to the common Schedule K insurance question.
prompt: I interned in Quebec from January to June 2025. Tax software asks whether I had basic prescription drug insurance through a group plan. Should I answer Yes?

recommendation.answer: Do not answer Yes just because you had an internship. Answer Yes only if your employer, school, spouse, parent, or another group plan actually covered basic prescription drugs for the relevant months.
recommendation.rationale: Quebec's prescription drug insurance question is about real coverage, not just employment status. The safe path is to map each month to RAMQ, private/group coverage, or an exemption before choosing the software answer.

required_evidence.description: Employer or school benefits booklet showing whether prescription drugs were covered.
Pay stub deductions or insurer portal record for the internship months.

assumptions: The internship alone does not prove drug coverage.
risks: Answering Yes without coverage evidence can understate the Quebec prescription drug insurance premium.
Answering No when group coverage existed can also produce an incorrect filing position.
recommendation.next_step: Check the employer benefits record and build a month-by-month coverage table before filing.

title: Tuition carryforward
tagline: Why a large unused tuition amount does not become a cash refund.
prompt: I have about 100,000 dollars of unused tuition credits. Why did my refund not increase by 100,000 dollars?

recommendation.answer: Unused tuition is not a cash refund balance. It is generally a non-refundable credit that can reduce tax payable when you have enough taxable income.
recommendation.rationale: A non-refundable credit lowers tax payable, but it usually cannot create a refund beyond tax already withheld or refundable credits. In a low-income year, much of the carryforward may remain unused.

required_evidence.description: CRA notice of assessment showing the unused tuition carryforward.
T4/RL slips and generated return summary showing income, tax payable, and tax withheld.

assumptions: The amount refers to unused tuition/education amounts, not tax withheld.
risks: Confusing credit amount with refund amount can lead to unrealistic refund expectations.
Software may use only the portion needed to reduce tax payable for the year.
recommendation.next_step: Compare tax payable before credits, tax withheld, and remaining carryforward on the generated forms.

title: New PR and RAMQ timeline
tagline: Separate card arrival, eligibility, and month-by-month coverage.
prompt: I became a permanent resident in July and received my RAMQ card in October. How should I think about the Quebec prescription drug insurance premium?

recommendation.answer: Do not treat the physical card date as the whole answer. Build a month-by-month timeline using the RAMQ eligibility or registration date, any private coverage, and any exemption periods.
recommendation.rationale: The tax software is trying to determine which months were covered by a qualifying plan or subject to the public plan premium. Immigration status, RAMQ registration, and card mailing date can be different facts.

required_evidence.description: RAMQ letter or online account showing the effective coverage or registration date.
Any private or group insurance card for months before RAMQ coverage.

assumptions: The user was a Quebec resident for at least part of the year.
risks: Using the card arrival date instead of the effective date may misclassify months.
Revenu Quebec may cross-check official coverage records.
recommendation.next_step: Create a 12-row month table and mark RAMQ, group/private insurance, or no coverage for each month.

title: Tax software discrepancy
tagline: When TurboTax and Wealthsimple ask different questions.
prompt: TurboTax asks about a credit but Wealthsimple Tax does not show the same question. Which software is right?

recommendation.answer: Do not assume either product is right from the interview question alone. Identify the underlying form or line, then compare the generated forms and the eligibility facts.
recommendation.rationale: Tax software products can use different interview flows. One may ask explicitly while another infers the answer, hides it until conditions are met, or leaves it in a forms view.

required_evidence.description: Screenshots or exported summaries showing the exact question and any generated form line.
The official form or guide for the credit or premium in question.

assumptions: Both products are being compared for the same tax year and province.
risks: A missing interview question may still produce a correct form entry.
A visible interview question may be conditional and not prove eligibility.
recommendation.next_step: Find the generated form line in both products, then compare the facts each product used.

title: Manual tax situation intake
tagline: Turn entered facts into a filing checklist and form-review plan.
prompt: I want to manually enter sample facts: Quebec resident for 2025, internship income, unused tuition, and uncertain drug insurance coverage. What would TaxAgent analyze before filing?

recommendation.answer: TaxAgent would first normalize the entered facts into a filing checklist: province and residency dates, employment slips, tuition carryforward, drug insurance months, missing evidence, and the form lines that need review.
recommendation.rationale: Manual intake is useful when the user does not want to upload documents or when slips are incomplete. The system should separate known facts, missing evidence, assumptions, and software/form decisions before giving filing guidance.

required_evidence.description: T4/RL-1 or employment summary for income and tax withheld.
CRA/Revenu Quebec notice showing carryforward balances.
Benefits or RAMQ evidence for each month of Quebec drug insurance coverage.

assumptions: The facts are sample facts for a public demo, not real filing data.
The user wants analysis and form-review help before submission.
risks: A manual form can omit slip boxes or official carryforward balances.
Unverified insurance months can produce the wrong Quebec premium treatment.
recommendation.next_step: Review the generated checklist, attach sample slips if available, then compare the suggested form lines before filing.

title: Sample tax slip review
tagline: Preview how uploaded slips become extracted facts and filing checks.
prompt: Use sample T4, RL-1, and T2202 slips to show what TaxAgent would extract and what it would check before helping with the return.

recommendation.answer: For the public demo, TaxAgent can simulate slip review by showing extracted sample facts, cross-checks, missing fields, and the filing questions those slips trigger. Real files should stay private unless live mode is explicitly enabled in a controlled setting.
recommendation.rationale: Slip review should not stop at OCR. The product value is mapping document fields to tax facts, detecting gaps, and explaining which form decisions depend on those facts.

facts_used.value: local filename only in public demo

required_evidence.description: A controlled private upload or sample slip set for extraction.
Prior notices for carryforward balances and account-level confirmations.

assumptions: The public demo does not upload or parse real files.
The sample slip facts are illustrative and not personal tax data.
risks: OCR alone can misread boxes, provinces, and tax withheld amounts.
A slip review must be reconciled against CRA/Revenu Quebec records before submission.
recommendation.next_step: Use the sample slip buttons to demonstrate extraction, then show how missing evidence becomes a checklist before filing.
